newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian court orders Lebed to pay foe one rouble.
newsitem.headline: Russian court orders Lebed to pay foe one rouble.

text.p: A Russian court ordered former security adviser Alexander Lebed on Friday to pay one rouble (less than one cent) in damages to Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov in a libel case, Interfax news agency said.

The newspaper Argumenty i Fakty fared less well. It was ordered to pay 100 million roubles (about $18,000) after publishing comments by Lebed which the court decided were a slur to Kulikov's professional reputation.
"The court ruled that the information published in the weekly Argumenty i Fakty was incorrect and defamed Kulikov's honour, dignity and professional reputation," Interfax said.
In remarks published by Argumenty i Fakty last October, Lebed accused Kulikov of "doctoring Chechnya's accounts". Kulikov had denied the charge and launched legal proceedings.
Interfax said Kulikov intended to donate the money from Argumenty i Fakty to the families of interior ministry troops killed and wounded in the conflict in rebel Chechnya.
Kulikov and Lebed became bitter enemies during the latter's four-month tenure last year as national security adviser and secretary of Russia's influential security council.
President Boris Yeltsin eventually sacked Lebed last October, accusing him of openly harbouring presidential ambitions and of lacking team spirit.
Lebed won a court case against Kulikov last December after the interior minister accused him of preparing an armed mutiny. Kulikov was also fined the symbolic sum of one rouble.
